description: Canonical puzzle/solution catalog plus replay-backed fragment flow, transplantable fragment geometry and observed relative transforms for Opus Magnum Codex.

identity.canonicalStructuralHash: translation/rotation invariant hash preserving program timing
identity.canonicalMechanismHash: translation/rotation invariant hash with normalized program timing
identity.puzzleFeatureFingerprint: hash of solver-relevant puzzle chemistry, molecule topology, available parts and production constraints

fragmentIndex.purpose: Catalog reusable fragment mechanisms with representative canonical geometry.

fragmentFlowIndex.purpose: Catalog replay-observed transitions, same-solution convergence motifs and relative anchor transforms.

relativeTransform.delta: target anchor axial displacement rotated into the source anchor's local orientation

transitionAggregation.preferred: most frequently observed relative transform weighted by edge observationCount
transitionAggregation.variants: relative transform plus weighted observation count

fragmentFlowIndex.convergenceMotifs: sample evidence retains each concrete predecessor-to-target relative transform

geometryTransplant.purpose: Combine canonical fragment geometry with historically observed relative transforms to place connected mechanisms in a common coordinate frame.
nextValidation: propagate anchor transforms through an assembly DAG
materialize all representative fragment parts into one coordinate frame
detect conflicting placements and merge identical shared parts
write and validate a candidate solution
limitations: A preferred relative transform is an empirical prior and may have multiple historical variants.
Anchor-relative compatibility does not guarantee full-fragment non-overlap.
Program synchronization and collision validation remain downstream responsibilities.
